skill.name: ui-design-system
skill.description: UI design system toolkit for generating design tokens, documenting component rules, planning responsive behavior, and preparing developer handoff materials.
skill.summary: Generate design system tokens and guidance for consistent UI implementation.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: All three static findings are false positives caused by design-system terminology and Markdown command formatting. No evidence of shell execution, system reconnaissance, prompt injection, network access, or data exfiltration was found in the reviewed files.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 15 defines an 8px base spacing unit for a design grid. It does not inspect the host system or collect environment information.
The backticks are Markdown formatting around a documented local Python usage command. The script itself does not invoke shell commands or pass user input to a shell.
Line 29 describes an 8pt spacing grid as a design-system feature. This is not system reconnaissance and contains no host inspection behavior.

content.value_statement: Design systems lose consistency when tokens and component rules are scattered. This skill generates token structures and handoff guidance for UI teams.
actual_capabilities: Generates color palettes from a brand color, including primary, secondary, neutral, semantic, and surface tokens.
Creates typography scales, font presets, font weights, line heights, letter spacing, and text styles.
Builds spacing, sizing, border, shadow, animation, breakpoint, and z-index token groups.
Exports generated tokens as JSON, CSS custom properties, or SCSS variables.
Supports design system planning for component architecture, accessibility, and developer handoff.
limitations: The generator uses fixed presets for modern, classic, and playful styles.
It does not inspect existing design files or synchronize with Figma automatically.
It prints output to the terminal and does not write package files by default.
Generated tokens need human review for brand fit and accessibility contrast.

use_cases.title: Create a Token Baseline
use_cases.description: Generate a first token set from a brand color before building a new product interface.

use_cases.title: Prepare Engineering Handoff
use_cases.description: Convert design decisions into token groups that frontend engineers can review and implement.

use_cases.title: Standardize Responsive Rules
use_cases.description: Define breakpoint, sizing, spacing, and z-index conventions for reusable application components.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Basic Tokens
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new product style guide.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to generate modern design tokens for brand color #2563EB. Summarize the color, typography, and spacing choices.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Style Directions
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of multiple visual directions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate token recommendations for modern, classic, and playful styles. Explain which direction best fits a professional SaaS dashboard.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Component Standards
prompt_templates.scenario: Design system planning for reusable interface components.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create component standards for buttons, inputs, cards, shadows, and breakpoints using generated tokens. Include accessibility review points.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Full Handoff
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced handoff from design system strategy to frontend implementation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a complete design token handoff plan for a multi-brand application. Include naming rules, review steps, and implementation risks.

output_examples.input: Generate a modern token set from a blue brand color.
output: A primary and secondary color palette with neutral and semantic color groups.
A typography scale with font families, weights, line heights, and text styles.
Spacing, sizing, breakpoint, shadow, animation, and z-index groups ready for review.

output_examples.input: Prepare developer handoff guidance for generated tokens.
output: A concise handoff checklist for token naming, export format, accessibility review, and frontend adoption.
A list of implementation notes for CSS variables, SCSS variables, and design documentation.

output_examples.input: Evaluate whether playful tokens fit an enterprise dashboard.
output_examples.output: A design review that compares visual tone, component density, accessibility risk, and maintainability before recommending a safer style direction.

best_practices: Start with a verified brand color and review semantic colors against accessibility goals.
Keep token names stable before sharing them with engineering teams.
Run generated output through design and frontend review before adoption.
anti_patterns: Treating generated tokens as final brand guidance without design review.
Mixing generated token names with unrelated naming systems.
Using every generated scale value in production components.

faq.question: What does this skill generate?
faq.answer: It generates design token structures for colors, typography, spacing, sizing, borders, shadows, animation, breakpoints, and z-index.

faq.question: Which export formats are supported?
faq.answer: The included generator can export tokens as JSON, CSS custom properties, or SCSS variables.

faq.question: Can it replace a design system team?
faq.answer: No. It provides structured starting points that designers and engineers should review before production use.

faq.question: Does it connect to design tools automatically?
faq.answer: No. The reviewed files do not include Figma, Sketch, or repository synchronization.

faq.question: Is it useful for accessibility work?
faq.answer: It can organize accessibility review points, but teams must still verify contrast, focus states, and component behavior.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Product designers, design systems leads, and frontend engineers can use it to align token decisions and handoff details.
